original_idea.body:
# Compounding Failure: Social Engineering Capability × AI-Generated Deepfakes — Measuring Amplified Phishing Success Rates

**Problem:** Two interacting failure modes: (1) AI generates highly convincing spear phishing text (54% click-through rate, matching human attackers), and (2) AI voice/video deepfakes can impersonate known individuals. Combined, these create a multi-modal social engineering attack where text, voice, and video reinforce each other. The compounding effect on victim susceptibility is unmeasured.

**Direction:** Design a controlled study (using fictional personas with explicit participant consent) comparing: (A) AI text-only phishing, (B) AI text + automated voice deepfake call (using a free TTS service, not actual deepfakes), (C) human-crafted baseline. Use scenario rating scales for quality assessment rather than live deception. Measure believability scores from human raters for each condition.

**Why it matters:** Multi-modal social engineering may be qualitatively more dangerous than single-modal attacks (text or voice alone). Measuring the amplification factor informs whether combining modalities requires coordinated defensive responses beyond email filters alone.

**Relevant context:** Frontiers 2026: agentic AI automates spear phishing and 'generates convincing deepfake voice calls to extract sensitive information'. Hoxhunt 2025: AI phishing 24% more effective than humans. KnowBe4 2025 Phishing Industry Benchmark. No study measures multi-modal compounding. Darknet.org 2025 survey of generative AI in social engineering.
